topic.title: Data Handling and Your Responsibilities
topic.shortdesc: Where your content goes during translation, and what to check before you commit translated files.

body.p: Translation in is a reviewed, revertible workflow: the agent proposes translated files in your workspace, and nothing becomes part of your project until you commit it. The points below explain where your content goes and what to check before you do.

section.title: Where Your Content Goes
section.p: To translate content, sends the relevant source content to an AI provider that performs the translation, so content leaves the infrastructure during a translation job. The provider is engaged under terms that provide for zero data retention, so it does not retain your content for its own use after the request is served.
The authoritative description of how your data is processed is your Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

section.title: Translations Are Proposed Changes to Review
section.p: Like any translation, whether human or machine, a translated file can contain errors, including phrasing that changes the intended meaning. treats translated files the same way it treats any other proposed change: they land in your workspace for you to review before you commit them.
You are responsible for reviewing and verifying translated content before you publish it. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit for how to review effectively.

section.title: Review the Full Set of Changed Files
section.p: Because translation works by writing files into your workspace, a translation job can, in principle, change more than the translated prose. When you review a job's output, look at the complete set of changed files, not only the translated topics, and watch for changes beyond the translation itself, for example to publishing templates, to build or tool configuration, or to markup that affects the published output.

This is the same review discipline you would apply to any external contribution to your repository: read the changed files before committing them. Because the changes arrive as ordinary workspace edits, you can inspect, adjust, or discard any of them before they become part of your project.
